meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (investor home jurisdiction; WFOE to be incorporated in mainland China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law hybridizing socialist-market statutory overlay in mainland China and Civil Law in Taiwan; cross-strait bilateral instruments govern inter-regional corporate and evidentiary matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Bilateral Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (ARATS-SEF, signed 2012-08-09, effective 2013-02-01)
Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA, signed 2010-06-29, effective 2010-09-12)
Agreement on the Use and Verification of Notarized Certificates Across the Straits (signed 1993-04-29, effective 1993-05-29)

Cross-Strait Taxation Agreement (signed 2009-12-10; double-taxation relief chapters ratified but not yet effective; administrative tax information exchange applied on a reciprocal administrative basis)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC (adopted 2006-12-27, fully revised 2025-04-25, effective 2026-01-01); PBOC Order No. 1 [2021] 'Measures for Supervision and Administration of Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing of Financial Institutions'; UBO: PBOC-SAMR Order No. 3 [2024] 'Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information' (effective 2024-11-01), administered jointly by PBOC and SAMR through the national Beneficial Owner Information System; Investment: Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (effective 2020-01-01), MOFCOM-SAMR Order No. 2 [2019] 'Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures', and the Law on the Protection of Investment by Taiwanese Compatriots (1994, amended 2019); Company Law of the PRC (2023 revision, effective 2024-07-01) Article 47 requires full payment of subscribed registered capital within 5 years of incorporation for limited liability companies, with no statutory minimum capital for this industry; Taiwan-invested WFOEs are registered as foreign-invested enterprises with a Taiwan investment marker in the SAMR registration system.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: beneficial owner data is filed with the PBOC-SAMR national UBO registry at incorporation and is accessible to PBOC, SAMR, tax, customs, and obliged financial institutions under statutory authority; not publicly searchable, and nominee arrangements are pierced by look-through rules under Order No. 3 [2024].

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Taiwan Certificate of Company Registration and extract of incorporation (公司登記證明書暨設立/變更登記表) of the Taiwanese investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (經濟部商業發展署)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Notarization Verification per the 1993 ARATS-SEF Agreement: Taiwan court notary or licensed private notary public -> Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification and forwarding -> ARATS-coordinated provincial notary association verification in mainland China -> certified Chinese translation; NOT Hague Apostille (Taiwan is not a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) and NOT Consular Legalization (no diplomatic relations between mainland China and Taiwan)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of directors and shareholders / share register of the Taiwanese investing company (董事暨股東名冊)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs registry extract, notarized by a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Notarization Verification (Taiwan notary -> SEF -> ARATS provincial notary association verification) followed by certified Chinese translation; neither Apostille nor consular legalization is applicable to Taiwan-issued instruments

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the mainland China incorporation agent and designated legal representative of the WFOE (委託書)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan notary public (court-affiliated or private notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Notarization Verification (Taiwan notary -> SEF -> ARATS provincial notary association verification) with certified Chinese translation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 17, 18, 20, 129-156, 159-169, 192-202, 216-227, 387 and 393; Foreign Investment Act, including Articles 4, 6, 8 and 9; Business Registration Act; and Regulations Governing Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent municipal government commercial registration authority, depending on the registered office location; foreign investment approval is handled by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration, together with Foreign Investment Approval Application and Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares or company limited by shares wholly owned by foreign investors. The subscribed capital must be sufficient for the proposed business, and a Taiwan-certified public accountant must verify the capital contribution after remittance. Capital is normally remitted into a designated bank account and converted into Taiwan dollars; there is no universal statutory escrow requirement, but the bank account and remittance evidence must be maintained for capital verification and foreign-investment reporting. The stated fee is approximately USD 22 based on the standard electronic company-registration fee of NT$700 and is exchange-rate dependent; name reservation, certification, translation, investment approval, and other charges may apply separately.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and record the sole shareholder’s subscription for all issued shares stated in the incorporation application, subject to receipt and certification of the subscribed capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at the address approved by the competent authority is adopted as the Company’s principal office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] is appointed General Manager, and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each to serve in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and applicable Taiwan law. Any director is authorized to complete filings, banking, licensing, and implementation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Foreign Investment Eligibility and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion and the competent company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the foreign investor is not restricted or prohibited under Taiwan’s negative-list rules. Conduct company-name and business-scope checks, including manufacturing of orthopedic medical devices and any controlled medical-device activities. Ensure the proposed articles, capital structure, directors, registered office, and business-purpose codes are consistent with the investment application.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation or equivalent constitutional document
Foreign investor ownership and ultimate-beneficial-owner information
Power of attorney for Taiwan representative or agent
Proposed company name and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the authority’s written query within the stated cure period, amend the business scope or ownership documents if required, and resubmit the corrected application. A refusal may generally be challenged through the applicable administrative appeal and litigation procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Investment Promotion online or paper filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application before capital remittance and company registration. Submit certified corporate documents, ownership information, investment plan, proposed capital amount, business activities, source-of-funds information, and power of attorney. Foreign documents must be notarized or authenticated as applicable, legalized through the competent Taiwan representative office where required, and translated into Chinese.
required_dossiers: Shareholder or board approval authorizing the investment
Passport or identification documents of responsible persons
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies identified by the Department of Investment Promotion, provide supplementary ownership or source-of-funds evidence, and obtain any required sectoral clearance. Do not remit or deploy investment capital until approval is issued unless a specific lawful exception applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Name and Complete Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce company-name and business-scope reservation system or competent municipal commercial registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the Chinese company name and confirm permissible business purposes. Execute the Articles of Incorporation, shareholder subscription documents, director consents, registered-office consent, and incorporation application. Have foreign signatures notarized or authenticated in the jurisdiction of execution and provide certified Chinese translations.
required_dossiers: Company name and business-scope reservation result
Share subscription or investment commitment documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace unavailable or misleading company names, correct prohibited business-purpose wording, and refile the reservation or incorporation package. Preserve the reservation before its expiry date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Remit Capital and Obtain CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-designated receiving bank and Taiwan-certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the designated capital account, remit the approved investment amount through traceable banking channels, retain SWIFT records and bank credit advice, and convert or deposit the funds as required. Engage a Taiwan-certified public accountant to examine the bank evidence, subscription records, and capital amount and issue the capital verification report.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remittance descriptions, currency conversion, account-holder, or amount discrepancies through the receiving bank. If the remittance exceeds or differs from the approved investment, obtain amended approval before registration or capital deployment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent local municipal government commercial registration authority or Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company-registration application electronically or at the competent counter with the approved Articles, capital verification, investor approval, director information, registered-office evidence, and statutory fee. The application must identify the responsible person and comply with the selected Taiwan company form. Obtain the company registration number and approval certificate before commencing ordinary business operations.
required_dossiers: Company seal and responsible-person seal specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registrar’s deficiency notice, submit corrected forms or missing evidence, and pay any additional fee. If rejected, request written reasons and use the applicable administrative appeal route after correcting the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Bank, Labor, and Beneficial-Ownership Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, local tax office, designated bank, Bureau of Labor Insurance, National Health Insurance Administration, and competent labor authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for business-tax and tax-filing purposes, activate the corporate bank account, register labor and health-insurance accounts when employees are hired, and establish accounting, invoice, payroll, withholding, and record-retention controls. Register the responsible person and maintain ultimate-beneficial-owner and shareholder records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax-registration or address inconsistencies, provide additional premises evidence, and respond to tax-office inspection requests. Late registration may create tax, invoice, employment, or penalty exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Governance Records and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company’s board, shareholders, certified public accountant, and competent company-registration authority where filings are required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, approve officers, banking authority, accounting policies, registered office, seal custody, licensing program, and delegated signing authority. Maintain minutes, shareholder register, director and supervisor register, capital records, accounting books, related-party records, and annual filing calendar. File changes to directors, capital, office, or business scope within statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify defective resolutions where legally permissible, convene a corrective meeting, amend the relevant registration, and file late or corrected changes with supporting explanations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with the competent local government factory-registration authority and the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration for medical-device regulation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate under the Factory Management Act; Medical Device Manufacturing License or manufacturing approval under the Medical Devices Act; Medical Device Quality Management System compliance approval; and product registration or listing approval for each applicable orthopedic implant.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Ministry of Environment, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. A full EIA report is required only if the proposed site, factory scale, development type, emissions, land-use change, or other characteristics fall within a listed EIA category or threshold; otherwise, an EIA registration, environmental review, or exemption may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain wastewater discharge, air-pollution, waste, and hazardous-material approvals before operation where applicable. Comply with Taiwan Effluent Standards for process wastewater, Air Pollution Control Act requirements for particulate matter, metal dust, acid or solvent emissions and VOCs, and Waste Disposal Act requirements for classification, storage, manifests, licensed transport, and treatment of metal powder, contaminated filters, chemical residues, sludge, and other industrial waste. Install dust collection, ventilation, wastewater treatment, spill containment, and monitoring systems according to the approved permit conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain building-use and occupancy approvals, factory-registration inspection, and fire-safety inspection or approval from the competent local fire authority. Provide structural-load verification for additive-manufacturing equipment, powder-storage areas, lifting equipment, gas cylinders, and clean or controlled production areas. Complete occupational safety and health risk assessments, machinery guarding, hazardous-chemical controls, explosion and combustible-powder controls, emergency response plans, worker training, and required labor-inspection clearances under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and related regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局, 'SAT'), headquartered in Beijing; administrative supervision is exercised by the municipal SAT branch at the WFOE's registered address. All registrations, filings, invoice clearance and export refund functions are executed through the SAT Electronic Tax Bureau portal ('电子税务局', https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn), the national VAT invoice service platform, and the Golden Tax IV ('金税四期') system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the WFOE at the Municipal Market Supervision Administration (市场监督管理局) to obtain the business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code ('统一社会信用代码'), which simultaneously becomes the statutory tax registration number via SAT-SAMR data linkage; tax registration is deemed completed upon license issuance, with a 30-day supplementary filing grace period. (2) File taxpayer commencement and tax-type determination (税种认定) through the E-Tax Bureau to fix the applicable VAT taxpayer type (General or Small-Scale), Enterprise Income Tax, urban maintenance and education surcharges, stamp duty, and payroll withholding taxes. (3) Register the legal representative, financial officer and tax agent; bind the corporate digital certificate; procure the e-Tax UKey (税务UKey); and activate fully digitalized electronic invoicing (数电票). (4) For export operations: complete the MOFCOM foreign-trade operator filing (对外贸易经营者备案), customs exporter registration (海关进出口收发货人备案), NMPA medical-device export recordation, and bank goods-trade FX account settlement. (5) File the export tax refund qualification ('出口退税备案') and designate the 'exemption-credit-refund' (免抵退) method applicable to manufacturing exporters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (worldwide-income resident enterprise; no pass-through eligibility). The WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise ('居民企业') taxed at the all-in 25% Enterprise Income Tax rate on worldwide income; it is a separate taxable person distinct from its foreign shareholders and cannot consolidate with them. Dividends remitted to a Taiwan-resident shareholder attract 10% withholding, potentially reduced to 5% only where the Cross-Strait Tax Cooperation Agreement applies and Taiwan-resident beneficial ownership is substantiated. Indirectly, the WFOE is a VAT taxpayer, customs duty payer, urban surcharge taxpayer and stamp duty taxpayer. No tax-exempt-zone entity status attaches merely from location in a bonded zone; any zone-based preferences operate at transactional level only.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) VAT status election: annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 compel General VAT Taxpayer status; smaller enterprises may elect General status voluntarily or remain Small-Scale Taxpayers (3% levy with periodic preferential reductions). (b) Export method: manufacturing WFOEs are statutorily bound to the 'exemption-credit-refund' (免抵退) formula; no election exists to use the trading-company 'exemption-refund' (免退) method unless the entity is restructured as a trading company. (c) EIT planning: no check-the-box regime in the U.S. sense; available elections are limited to special tax treatment of qualifying asset reorganizations, statutory 5-year EIT loss carryforward utilization, and Advanced Pricing Arrangements for related-party export pricing; hybrid instrument and beneficial-ownership positions are governed by the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and filing disclosures. (d) Small-scale taxpayers may elect to waive statutory VAT exemptions in order to issue special VAT invoices deductible by customers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (增值税, 'VAT') with a parallel Consumption Tax (消费税) on a narrow goods list not applicable to titanium orthopedic implants; export sales of goods are zero-rated through the exemption-credit-refund mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Every WFOE with a business license is automatically VAT-registered; China imposes no economic-turnover threshold permitting exemption from registration. The operative threshold is the General versus Small-Scale taxpayer status line: annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (approximately USD 690,000) compel General VAT Taxpayer registration; below this line the entity defaults to Small-Scale Taxpayer status (3% levy) unless it elects General status. For the titanium implant manufacturer, General Taxpayer status is functionally indispensable because only General Taxpayers may claim input VAT credit and export refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance under the fully digitalized e-invoice (数电票) and Golden Tax IV regime: every VAT invoice is issued through the E-Tax Bureau using the taxpayer's digital certificate; the national platform validates each invoice block online, assigns a 26-digit anti-counterfeit code, and records it instantaneously for the buyer's input-credit eligibility. Physical stamping is not required for fully digitalized invoices; paper-plus-seal invoices survive only in transitional scenarios. Large taxpayers may apply for the '乐企' direct-connection API integrating SAT clearance inside the enterprise ERP; all other taxpayers use the web portal. The system performs real-time triangulation of invoice flow, payment flow, logistics flow and, for exports, customs declaration data; any anomaly automatically suspends invoice quotas or export refund processing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% output VAT with credit and refund of input VAT) is available only where all of the following criteria are satisfied: (i) Exporter status — the WFOE holds a valid foreign-trade operator filing, customs exporter registration, NMPA Medical Device Production License (医疗器械生产许可证), and export recordation for the porous titanium hip implant classified under HS 9021.31; (ii) Physical export — the goods are declared at a PRC customs port and leave the customs territory of the People's Republic of China for Taiwan or another destination; Taiwan is treated by PRC customs as a separate customs territory, so a full mainland export clearance is mandatory; the customs declaration names the WFOE as consignor and states the true FOB value; (iii) Genuine foreign sale — a valid export contract, commercial invoice and packing list with an overseas or Taiwanese purchaser, identical in quantity, unit price, product description and value; (iv) FX repatriation — export proceeds are received through a designated bank and reported under the goods-trade Foreign Exchange monitoring system; (v) Input VAT chain — the WFOE maintains compliant special VAT invoices for titanium alloy powder feedstock, electron-beam 3D-printing consumables, electricity and production equipment so that the refund is confined to VAT economically borne on the exported production; (vi) Timely filing — the monthly 'exemption-credit-refund' application is filed within the statutory period following the month of customs export; separate cross-border-service zero-rating rules apply to any offshore engineering or consulting services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单) — electronic customs record with HS 9021.31 classification, FOB value and export port, naming the WFOE as exporter
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (海运提单/空运单) — third-party transport document evidencing that the goods left PRC customs territory and were destined for the Taiwanese buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Income Declaration (出口收汇确认凭证/涉外收入申报单) — bank confirmation that export proceeds were received and settled through the goods-trade FX monitoring system
Commercial Invoice, Packing List and Export Contract (商业发票、装箱单、外销合同) — complete product description, unit prices and export terms reconciling with the customs declared value
Medical Device Production License and Export Recordation File (医疗器械生产许可证及出口备案) — NMPA-issued documentary proof of lawful manufacture and market authorization for the titanium hip implant
Certificate of Origin and cross-strait trade documentation (原产地证书及两岸贸易单证) — required where Taiwan customs or the buyer-side certification demands origin evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export refund claims are machine-audited by the 'four-flow matching' (四流合一) engine reconciling contract flow, goods flow, invoice flow and payment flow; any mismatch triggers manual inspection or on-site audit. Legal consequences for fraudulent zero-rating or over-refund include: (i) clawback — SAT orders repayment of the entire refunded VAT plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; (ii) monetary penalty — 50% to 5 times the fraudulent refund amount under Articles 63 and 66 of the Tax Administration Law; (iii) unlimited recovery period — the ordinary 3-to-5-year statute of limitation does not apply to fraud or evasion, permitting indefinite retrospective clawback; (iv) criminal liability — Article 204 of the Criminal Law punishes fraudulent export tax refund with imprisonment and fines; (v) administrative sanctions — suspension or cancellation of the export tax refund qualification, revocation of foreign-trade operator status, inclusion in the national tax blacklist with consequential restrictions in banking, credit and customs AEO treatment; (vi) FX penalties — failure to repatriate proceeds within 180 days without a SAFE-approved exception attracts fines of 0.5% to 30% of the unrepatriated amount and retrospective denial of refund claims; (vii) EIT reassessment — if export prices are recharacterized as related-party transfer pricing misstatements, additional Enterprise Income Tax, interest and penalties are superimposed on the VAT clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC / 中国人民银行) as the central monetary authority; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE / 国家外汇管理局) as the direct foreign-exchange regulator; National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA / 国家金融监督管理总局) as the banking licensing and on-balance-sheet supervisor; Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM / 商务部) and National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC / 国家发展和改革委员会) as the investment-access gatekeepers under the Foreign Investment Law and the nationwide Negative List. SAFE administers the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (外汇管理条例), the Measures for the Administration of Foreign Exchange in Goods Trade (汇发〔2012〕38号), and the bank-delegated FDI registration framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible for current-account items (goods trade, services trade, wages, and qualifying profit/dividend remittances after tax settlement) pursuant to China's IMF Article VIII obligations, but every receipt or payment is subject to genuine-transaction verification (真实性审核) by a designated FX bank. Capital-account items remain selectively convertible: inbound FDI is liberalized and requires only post-establishment FDI registration (delegated to banks) plus compliance with the Foreign Investment Negative List (2023 edition), whereas outbound portfolio investment, cross-border guarantees, intra-group on-lending, and securities transactions remain quota- or approval-gated. Profit remittance to the Taiwan parent is a current-account transfer but carries filing hurdles: (i) the WFOE must evidence corporate income tax settlement via the tax payment receipt (完税证明); (ii) the board must pass a dividend declaration based on audit-adjusted PRC GAAP financials; (iii) the remitting bank requires the audited financial statement, tax clearance, and board resolution; and (iv) the remittance is legally subject to PRC withholding tax of 10% absent treaty relief (the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not yet ratified, so no effective reduction to 5% currently applies). These conditions must be satisfied before the bank will release the SWIFT MT103 outbound transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory FX surrender was abolished on 1 August 2012. Current rules: (1) no statutory conversion ratio applies to export receipts - an A-class goods-trade enterprise may freely retain hard currency in an FX current account or convert into RMB; (2) repatriation remains mandatory - export proceeds must be collected onshore through a designated FX bank within generally 180 days from the customs export declaration date (出口收汇期限), with any delay beyond 180 days requiring documented justification (e.g., extended open-account credit terms or payment disputes) and bank declaration; (3) the WFOE must complete SAFE goods-trade list registration (名录登记), operate under the total-quantity verification/balance-checking regime (总量核查), and promptly file all BOP receipts and payments; (4) if downgraded to B/C category, export proceeds must flow through a pending-receipt FX account (待核查账户) and the WFOE must present customs declarations, contracts, and invoices per transaction before settlement; (5) non-compliance triggers SAFE warnings, administrative penalties, suspension of FX settlement convenience, and downgrade to B/C status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Credit Information Report (企业年度报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in operating abnormal list; fine up to RMB 10,000; after three consecutive years of non-filing, placement on serious illegal list and risk of administrative revocation of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (外商投资信息报告年度报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via SAMR co-collection system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same window as SAMR annual report: 1 January to 30 June annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order to rectify and warning; administrative fine up to RMB 100,000 for late or inaccurate reporting; adverse effect on corporate credit and foreign investment qualifications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement Filing (企业所得税年度汇算清缴)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through competent local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to RMB 2,000; late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; additional penalty up to 50% of under-declared tax for fraudulent underpayment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Equity Annual Registration (境内直接投资外方权益存量登记)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for the previous fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Foreign exchange administrative penalties; inclusion in SAFE compliance blacklist; suspension or limitation of cross-border payments, dividend remittances, and foreign exchange account operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Taiwan Mainland-Investment Annual Report (大陆投资事业年度申报)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission (投資審議司)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 30 June for the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to NT$1,000,000 under the Regime for Cross-Strait Relations; subsequent mainland investment applications rejected; possible revocation or restriction of approved investment quota.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all wholly foreign-owned enterprises irrespective of revenue, total assets, or employee count; PRC Foreign Investment Law and Ministry of Finance rules require an independent annual audit by a Chinese CPA firm.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS is not accepted as the sole statutory reporting basis for PRC regulatory filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the WFOE must re-confirm ultimate actual controllers and full ownership chain in the Foreign Investment Information Annual Report and update SAMR registration for any shareholding changes. PRC anti-money-laundering rules require enhanced UBO identification and PEP screening during banking relationship maintenance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferences include a 15% reduced rate for High and New Technology Enterprises, a 5% effective rate for small low-profit enterprises on taxable income up to RMB 3 million, 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses, and accelerated depreciation or tax holiday for qualifying encouraged-technology medical device projects.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Category A) filed through the State Taxation Administration's Electronic Tax Bureau portal (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) or the local provincial e-taxing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional filings on Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within five months after the balance-sheet date (on or before May 31 of the following calendar year); quarterly provisional payments are due within fifteen days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from sales of titanium orthopedic hip implant prosthetics, including export sales to Taiwan and related processing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PRC-resident WFOE reports its worldwide business income; non-resident shareholders do not report on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consumption tax, city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, property tax, stamp duty and other business-related levies expensed in the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident participation; the line is completed using the WFOE's own ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting pre-tax profit computed under PRC GAAP, reflecting revenue less cost, expenses, asset impairments, gains and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the WFOE's entity-level figure; intercompany payments to the Taiwan parent must be supported by contractual substance and arm's-length valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding or deducting tax adjustments, offsetting prior-year losses, and applying permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributable profits planned for repatriation are not deductible; transfer-pricing and anti-avoidance adjustments must be incorporated here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable statutory rate (25% standard or 15% preferential rate for High and New Technology Enterprises).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate is applied at entity level; no line allocation to foreign shareholders is permissible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final annual tax due after deducting quarterly prepayments, foreign tax credits, and other withholdings; this amount is payable by the last filing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends distributed to the Taiwan parent are subject to additional withholding at the time of distribution; they are not included in this line.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a minimum penalty of RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 for repeat violations) plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax; underpayment due to false reporting is subject to a fine of 50% to 500% of the deficient tax and potential criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (withholding at source on dividends paid by the Chinese WFOE to the Taiwan corporate shareholder under EIT Law Art. 3 and Art. 37).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The 2015 Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Arrangement is not yet conclusively implemented in China's administrative enforcement; therefore the 10% statutory rate is currently applied. If the arrangement is invoked, the Taiwan parent must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the Taiwanese tax authority (Ministry of Finance) and file the tax-treaty benefit application with the China tax authority through the WFOE's Electronic Tax Bureau account, together with a beneficial ownership declaration, capital-holding evidence, and the related-party transaction disclosure forms. A reduced 5% rate on dividends may apply only after the arrangement is formally in effect and the Taiwan shareholder holds at least 25% of the paid-in capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate for interest and IP royalties paid by the WFOE to a Taiwanese non-resident enterprise is 10% each. In the absence of an effective cross-strait tax arrangement, no reduction is available; once the 2015 arrangement is operative, the treaty rate for interest and royalties would similarly be capped at 10%, subject to the same TRC and beneficial ownership documentation process.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared when any category of related-party transactions exceeds RMB 200 million for tangible assets, RMB 100 million for intangible assets, RMB 100 million for financial assets, or RMB 40 million for other transactions; Master File is mandatory if annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not operate formal Economic Substance Regulations of the kind seen in offshore finance centres; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Art. 47) and the Beneficial Ownership Test (Announcement 2018 No. 9) require the WFOE to demonstrate genuine business substance in China, including physical production facilities for titanium orthopedic implants, resident operational management, sufficient employees, and actual risk-control and decision-making functions. Failure to maintain substance can result in denial of tax incentives, recharacterisation of transactions, and imposition of a 25% tax on adjusted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of foreign sales of titanium prostheses, use of forged invoices, false declaration of intercompany management fees to the Taiwan parent, or concealment of SWIFT wire or letter-of-credit receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid corporate income tax plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Art. 201 provides imprisonment of three to seven years and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the statutory representative, and financial officers are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the unpaid tax if corporate formalities are abused; courts may impose exit bans, freeze personal assets, and order imprisonment of responsible individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Electron-beam 3D melting services and titanium implant-related IP are charged to the Taiwan parent at zero or artificial mark-ups; failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or to report related-party transactions on the annual return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under EIT Law Art. 123 with secondary adjustment, 50%–500% underpayment penalty, daily surcharge at 0.05%, an administrative fine up to RMB 50,000 for non-filing, and a ten-year retroactive assessment period for transfer pricing adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute fraudulent intercompany agreements or approve fictional royalties may be personally liable; in aggravated cases the authorities impose asset freezes, exit controls, and criminal liability for intentional mispricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE has no physical manufacturing line, holds no medical-device production license, employs no resident staff, and is used as a pass-through invoicing entity for the Taiwan parent to shift profits from mainland China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard the legal entity under GAAR, recharacterise the transactions, impose 25% EIT on imputed profits, revoke tax-preference treatment, levy penalties and interest, and refer the matter to customs and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange for blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Company Law Art. 20 exposes directors and shareholders to joint and several liability for unpaid corporate taxes; in serious cases, travel bans and imprisonment for illegal business operations or fraudulent dissolution are available.
